extracted.intended_audience: WHO communicators and public health communication practitioners (country, regional and headquarters offices)
extracted.subtask_description: A strategic communications framework describing principles and tactical guidance for designing, producing and evaluating WHO health communications so they are actionable, accessible, relevant, timely, understandable and credible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal and key audiences
rubrics_metrics.guidance: WHO communicates to and with key audiences - the agents who use WHO communications products to make a range of health decisions. Communications should be designed with these decision-makers in mind (policy-makers, health professionals, partners, and the public as appropriate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: Make information available online; identify effective channels; ensure accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make information available online and identify effective channels so target audiences can reach the information. Ensure accessibility (e.g., formats and channels that work for people with disabilities and variable internet/connectivity). Consider channel reach and ease of access when choosing how to publish content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Know the audience; listen to the audience; tailor the message; motivate the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand audience needs and context by listening and researching. Tailor messages to audience priorities and circumstances so content is meaningful and motivates the intended audiences to act or decide differently. Relevance requires audience segmentation and message personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionable
rubrics_metrics.description: Move audiences to action; design for behaviour change; communicate in emergencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications should aim to prompt clear, feasible actions by the audience. Use behaviour change campaign principles where appropriate and ensure emergency communications enable immediate and appropriate actions. Provide explicit calls to action and steps audiences can follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Communicate early; communicate at the right time; build the conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide information as early as possible and at the moments when audiences need it. Time messaging to align with decision points and opportunities to influence outcomes. Build ongoing conversations rather than one-off messages to maintain relevance and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credible
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical accuracy; be transparent; coordinate with partners; speak as 'One WHO'; respect WHO brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure technical accuracy in content and be transparent about evidence, uncertainty and limitations. Coordinate messaging with partners and across WHO offices to maintain consistent 'One WHO' voice. Use WHO branding and maintain standards that sustain institutional credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understandable
rubrics_metrics.description: Use plain language; tell real stories; make it visual; use familiar languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write in plain language and avoid jargon so messages are easily understood. Use storytelling, visuals and familiar/local languages to increase comprehension and engagement. Test messages for clarity with target audiences where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation is an important communication function at all levels of the Organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define evaluation as judging WHO messages, products, and engagements based on their effectiveness at reaching specified goals and principles. Use assessment/evaluation to measure whether communications are reaching goals (e.g., accessibility, relevance, actionability, timeliness, understandability, credibility). Embed evaluation questions into planning and update practice based on findings.
